=== comments: `;` anywhere, `#` at the start of a line
# a comment line
	.CSEG	TEXT
START:	MOV	A, #1		; trailing comment
	# indented comment
	NOP
--- gnu
	.text
START:	mov	a, #1
	nop
=== numbers: prefix, suffix and leading-zero octal
	.DB	0x1F, 0X1F, 1FH, 0FFh, 0b101, 101B, 074, 74O, 128, 0
--- gnu
	.byte	0x1f, 0x1f, 0x1f, 0xff, 5, 5, 60, 60, 128, 0
=== character constants and strings with escapes
	.DB	'A', ' ', '\n', '\'', "AB", "\x41\101\\", "q""q"
--- gnu
	.byte	0x41, 0x20, 10, 0x27, 0x41, 0x42, 0x41, 0x41, 0x5c, 0x71, 0x22, 0x71
=== operator precedence: shifts bind like `*`, `+` binds tighter than `&`
	.DB	1 + 2 << 1, 2 & 1 + 1, 6 | 1 ^ 3, 2 * 0x0F - 0x0B & 0x0A | 0x0F, 5+8-6*2/4
--- gnu
	.byte	5, 2, 4, 15, 10
=== relational and logical operators yield 0 or 1
	.DB	1 == 1, 1 != 1, 2 > 1, 2 >= 3, 1 < 2, 3 <= 2, 1 && 0, 1 || 0, 256 % 50
--- gnu
	.byte	1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 6
=== `>>` shifts the 32-bit value, and past 31 gives 0
	.DB4	0xFFFFFFFF >> 4, 1 >> 32
	.DB	0x01AF >> 5
--- gnu
	.long	0x0fffffff, 0
	.byte	0x0d
=== byte and word separators, with and without parentheses
	.DB	HIGH(0x1234), LOW(0x1234), HIGH 0x0FFFF, LOW(~3)
	.DB2	HIGHW(0x12345678), LOWW(0x12345678), LOWW 0x12345678 + 1
--- gnu
	.byte	0x12, 0x34, 0xff, 0xfc
	.short	0x1234, 0x5678, 0x5679
=== separators in instruction operands
	MOVW	AX, #HIGHW(0x12345678)
	MOVW	BC, #LOWW(0x12345678)
	MOV	A, #LOW(0x1234)
	MOV	A, #HIGH(0x1234)
--- gnu
	movw	ax, #0x1234
	movw	bc, #0x5678
	mov	a, #0x34
	mov	a, #0x12
=== .EQU and .SET
SYM1	.EQU	0x10
CNT	.SET	1
	MOV	A, #SYM1
	MOV	A, #CNT
CNT	.SET	CNT + 1
	MOV	A, #CNT
--- gnu
	mov	a, #0x10
	mov	a, #1
	mov	a, #2
=== data directives of every width
LABEL:	.DB	10, "ABC"
	.DB2	0x1234
	.DB4	0x12345678
	.DB8	0x1234567890ABCDEF
--- gnu
LABEL:	.byte	10, 0x41, 0x42, 0x43
	.short	0x1234
	.long	0x12345678
	.long	0x90abcdef, 0x12345678
=== .DS reserves zeroed bytes
	.DB	1
	.DS	3
	.DB	2
--- gnu
	.byte	1
	.space	3
	.byte	2
=== .ALIGN pads with zeros
	.DB	1
	.ALIGN	4
	.DB	2
	.ALIGN	2
	.DB	3
--- gnu
	.byte	1
	.balign	4, 0
	.byte	2
	.balign	2, 0
	.byte	3
=== .OFFSET moves to an offset from the section start
	.DB	1
	.OFFSET	4
	.DB	2
--- gnu
	.byte	1
	.org	4
	.byte	2
=== $IF, $ELSEIF, $ELSE and $ENDIF
SW	.SET	2
$IF SW == 1
	.DB	1
$ELSEIF SW == 2
	.DB	2
$ELSE
	.DB	3
$ENDIF
 $ IFN SW
	.DB	4
 $ ELSEIFN SW - 2
	.DB	5
 $ ENDIF
--- gnu
	.byte	2
	.byte	5
=== $IFDEF and $IFNDEF, nested inside a false branch
DEFINED	.EQU	1
$IFDEF DEFINED
	.DB	1
$ENDIF
$IFNDEF DEFINED
	.DB	2
$IF 1
	.DB	3
$ENDIF
$ELSE
	.DB	4
$ENDIF
--- gnu
	.byte	1
	.byte	4
=== .MACRO with parameters, and `?` concatenation
LAB5	.EQU	0x55
ADMAC	.MACRO	PARA1, PARA2
	MOV	A, #PARA1
	ADD	A, #PARA2
	.DB	LAB?PARA1
	.ENDM
	ADMAC	5, 0x20
--- gnu
	mov	a, #5
	add	a, #0x20
	.byte	0x55
=== a parameter is a whole word, and strings and comments are left alone
X	.MACRO	A1
	.DB	A1, "A1"	; A1
	.DB	A12
	.ENDM
A12	.EQU	9
	X	7
--- gnu
	.byte	7, 0x41, 0x31
	.byte	9
=== .LOCAL gives each expansion its own label
M1	.MACRO	PAR
	.LOCAL	AA, BB
AA:	.DB	PAR
	BR	$AA
BB:	.DB	BB - AA
	.ENDM
	M1	1
	M1	2
--- gnu
L1:	.byte	1
	br	$L1
L2:	.byte	L2 - L1
L3:	.byte	2
	br	$L3
L4:	.byte	L4 - L3
=== .REPT and .IRP end with .ENDM, and nest in a macro
	.REPT	2 + 1
	INC	B
	.ENDM
	.IRP	PAR 0x10, 0x20
	ADD	A, #PAR
	.ENDM
TWICE	.MACRO	V
	.REPT	2
	.DB	V
	.ENDM
	.ENDM
	TWICE	7
--- gnu
	inc	b
	inc	b
	inc	b
	add	a, #0x10
	add	a, #0x20
	.byte	7, 7
=== .EXITM leaves the innermost repeat
	.REPT	3
	.REPT	2
	INC	B
	.EXITM
	.ENDM
	DEC	C
	.ENDM
--- gnu
	inc	b
	dec	c
	inc	b
	dec	c
	inc	b
	dec	c
=== [DE] and [HL] stand for a zero displacement where the manual lists it
	MOV	[DE], #1
	MOV	[HL], #2
	MOV	ES:[DE], #3
	MOVS	[HL], X
	CMPS	X, [HL]
	ADDW	AX, [HL]
	SUBW	AX, ES:[HL]
	CMPW	AX, [HL]
	INC	[HL]
	DEC	ES:[HL]
	INCW	[HL]
	DECW	[HL]
--- gnu
	mov	[de+0], #1
	mov	[hl+0], #2
	mov	es:[de+0], #3
	movs	[hl+0], x
	cmps	x, [hl+0]
	addw	ax, [hl+0]
	subw	ax, es:[hl+0]
	cmpw	ax, [hl+0]
	inc	[hl+0]
	dec	es:[hl+0]
	incw	[hl+0]
	decw	[hl+0]
=== operand sigils: #, !, !!, $, $!, ES: and bit positions
	.CSEG	TEXT
TOP:	MOV	A, !0xFE00
	MOV	ES:!0x1234, A
	MOV	A, 0xFFE30
	MOVW	AX, 0xFFF90
	BR	!!0x12345
	CALL	!0x1000
	BR	$TOP
	BR	$!TOP
	SET1	0xFFE20.3
	CLR1	A.5
	MOV1	CY, [HL].2
	BT	0xFFE21.0, $TOP
	MOV	A, [HL+B]
	MOV	A, 0x1234[B]
	MOV	A, ES:0x1234[BC]
--- gnu
TOP:	mov	a, !0xfe00
	mov	es:!0x1234, a
	mov	a, 0xffe30
	movw	ax, 0xfff90
	br	!!0x12345
	call	!0x1000
	br	$TOP
	br	$!TOP
	set1	0xffe20.3
	clr1	a.5
	mov1	cy, [hl].2
	bt	0xffe21.0, $TOP
	mov	a, [hl+b]
	mov	a, 0x1234[b]
	mov	a, es:0x1234[bc]
=== symbols may contain @ and $
A@B	.EQU	3
C$D	.EQU	4
@E:	.DB	A@B, C$D
--- gnu
	.byte	3, 4
=== the manual's own examples from the operator sections
	MOV	A, #2 * 3
	MOV	A, #250 / 50
	MOV	A, #256 % 50
	MOV	A, #LOW(~3)
	MOV	A, #0x6FA & 0x0F
	MOV	A, #0x0A | 0b1101
	MOV	A, #0x9A ^ 0x9D
	MOVW	AX, #0x01AF >> 5
	MOV	A, #0x21 << 2
	MOV	A, #(4 + 3) * 2
--- gnu
	mov	a, #6
	mov	a, #5
	mov	a, #6
	mov	a, #0xfc
	mov	a, #0x0a
	mov	a, #0x0f
	mov	a, #0x07
	movw	ax, #0x0d
	mov	a, #0x84
	mov	a, #14
